title: Basic LAN Connectivity Lab
objective: Build a single-switch local area network with three PCs, configure static IPv4 addresses within the same subnet, and verify connectivity using ICMP ping.

configurations.SW1:
enable
configure terminal
hostname SW1
banner motd # Authorized Access Only - Lab SW1 #
end
write memory

instructions: Open Cisco Packet Tracer and create a new workspace.
From Network Devices -> Switches, place one Cisco Catalyst 2960 switch labeled 'SW1'.
From End Devices, place three generic PCs labeled 'PC1', 'PC2', and 'PC3'.
Connect PC1 FastEthernet0 to SW1 FastEthernet0/1 using a Copper Straight-Through cable.
Connect PC2 FastEthernet0 to SW1 FastEthernet0/2 using a Copper Straight-Through cable.
Connect PC3 FastEthernet0 to SW1 FastEthernet0/3 using a Copper Straight-Through cable.
Wait ~30 seconds for the switch ports to transition from amber (Spanning Tree listening/learning) to green (forwarding), or click 'Fast Forward Time'.
Configure IP settings on each PC (Desktop -> IP Configuration):
Open SW1 CLI tab, press Enter, and paste the provided Cisco configuration to set the hostname and MOTD banner.
verification: Open PC1 Desktop -> Command Prompt and ping PC2: 'ping 192.168.1.20' (Expected: 4 replies, 0% packet loss).
From PC1 Command Prompt, ping PC3: 'ping 192.168.1.30' (Expected: 4 replies, 0% packet loss).
From PC2 Command Prompt, ping PC3: 'ping 192.168.1.30' (Expected: 4 replies, 0% packet loss).
On SW1 CLI, run 'show mac address-table' to verify that SW1 has learned the MAC addresses of PC1, PC2, and PC3.
